newsitem.title: USA: VLSI details image processor chip.
newsitem.headline: VLSI details image processor chip.

text.p: VLSI Technology Inc. on Monday outlined its custom graphics processing chip based on 0.35 micron process technology.

VLSI said the Image Memory Processor chip, which is used in Silicon Graphics Inc.'s Onyx2 InfiniteReality product, achieves extremely high circuit density levels and is used to convert polygon and texture data into pixels.
The IMP circuit integrates nearly 488,000 logic gates, or 1.95 million logic transistors, into a 6.5 by 6.5 mm core area, or a logic density of 11,540 logic gates per square mm.
This compares with between 6,120 and 8,590 gates per square mm for current-generation microprocessors, the company said in a statement released early Monday.
The company also said the given density is an average over the entire chip core area, and that the packing density within certain IMP circuit elements runs as high as 19,000 gates per square mm.

Silicon Graphics markets its Onyx2 InfiniteReality product, unveiled last October, as the world's fastest visualisation supercomputer, delivering 80 million polygons per second in its most powerful configuration.
